name: Colorado
standard: WCAG 2.1 A and AA (Digital Content); Section 508 Ch. 4 for hardware — per 8 CCR 1501-11

laws.summary: State and local public entities must meet OIT's technology accessibility standards, with civil remedies for violations.
Clarified enforcement and let OIT update standards to track WCAG.
Gave agencies showing good-faith efforts a one-year shield from liability, which expired 2025-07-01.

laws.cite: 8 CCR 1501-11 Rules Establishing Technology Accessibility Standards (amended, effective 2025-06-30)
laws.summary: OIT rules that set the technical standard, compliance options and accessibility statement duty.

laws.cite: 28 C.F.R. Part 35, Subpart H (ADA Title II web and mobile rule, 2024; dates extended by DOJ interim final rule 2026-04-20)
laws.summary: State and local governments must make web content and mobile apps conform to WCAG 2.1 AA.

applies_to: All public entities under C.R.S. § 24-34-301(18): state and local governments and their departments, agencies, special districts and instrumentalities; covers public- and internal-facing ICT, including through contractors.

deadlines.what: Rules apply to ICT in active use and ICT created or bought on or after this date
HB24-1454 good-faith liability grace period ended
Federal ADA Title II floor: public entities with population 50,000+ must meet WCAG 2.1 AA (extended from 2026-04-24)
Federal ADA Title II floor: entities under 50,000 and special districts (extended from 2027-04-26)

requires: Post a technology accessibility statement with more than one contact method and how to request accommodations and report barriers (11.6)

Comply through one of: meeting technical standards, a conforming alternate version, reasonable accommodations or modifications, a published Accessibility Plan updated annually, or best-meets procurement (11.5)
Exceptions for pre-2024 documents and social posts, third-party content, and archives (11.7)
mobile: explicit — the rules' 'Digital Content' definition names mobile applications.
procurement: Best-meets procurement is one compliance route; the rules cover ICT provided through contracts or licenses.
enforcement: Civil action under C.R.S. § 24-34-802 (injunctive relief and damages); secondary sources cite a $3,500 statutory penalty per violation.
notes: The $3,500 penalty and HB24-1454 details come from search results (leg.colorado.gov, CIRSA, Level Access), not a statute text that was opened. The federal Title II extension does not change Colorado's state deadline. Federal floor: ADA Title II rule (WCAG 2.1 AA, web + mobile apps) applies to all state and local government regardless of state law; DOJ's 2026-04-20 interim final rule moved compliance dates to 2027-04-26 / 2028-04-26.
